headline: High: shared writable workspace and B’s subprocess/network capabilities create default conflict and leakage risks; A is offline but can still feed unsafe content into B.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A can emit workflow/content artifacts and B reads files plus builds on shared context, so A’s outputs can be treated as instructions if bridged through files or copied text. A has no filesystem read/write or MCP, which limits direct injection, but B’s file ingestion and shared-skill pattern make the pathway plausible. Uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF A’s generated content is copied into a file that B reads as context, injection is possible.
IF B treats skill/context files as authoritative instructions, attacker-controlled text can steer behavior.
mitigations: Keep A and B in separate directories.
Require B to ignore instruction-like text in A outputs.
Add a manual review step before B consumes A-generated files.
Use a fixed template for A outputs with no free-form instructions.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between A and B.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A is offline and does not read files, while B can read/write files and use allowlisted egress. The pair can still leak marketing or workflow data if shared files contain sensitive material, but the blast radius is limited by A’s lack of filesystem access and B’s allowlisted network. This is a plausible but not default cross-agent exfiltration path.
conditions: IF shared files contain sensitive marketing context, B can read and transmit it to allowlisted services.
IF A-generated assets are stored in a shared workspace, B may ingest them into its context.
mitigations: Store sensitive inputs outside B’s workspace.
Restrict B’s allowlist to required domains only.
Review files before B uploads or references them.
Separate A-generated assets from B’s working directory.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: B has read/write filesystem plus subprocess and network egress, while A has no write or subprocess capability. There is no direct write-write collision, but if both are pointed at the same mutable workspace, B can overwrite or consume A’s generated artifacts and create coordination failures. Uncertainty about shared directories escalates this to medium.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to use the same writable directory, B can overwrite A’s outputs.
IF the orchestrator lacks locking, B may consume partially written artifacts from A.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Disable concurrent writes to shared paths.
Add file locks around shared artifacts.
Run B only after A finishes exporting outputs.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A produces creative outputs and workflow artifacts; B’s skill system explicitly builds on shared context, so B may treat A’s output as authoritative without verification. That creates a realistic cascade from A’s generated content into B’s marketing actions or deliverables. Because B is not documented as critically evaluating A, the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF B imports A-generated text or assets as source material, errors can propagate into downstream marketing work.
IF B lacks a verification step, hallucinated or malformed A outputs can be rendered as facts.
mitigations: Require source checks before B uses A outputs.
Have B cite provenance for every imported claim.
Use a human approval gate for downstream deliverables.
Limit A outputs to non-authoritative drafts.
requires-engineering: add automated fact/provenance validation.

E_compliance.rationale: No explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for either agent. A is open-source and offline-capable, while B uses allowlisted egress and shared skill files, so compliance risk is mainly operational rather than a proven policy conflict. Because the evidence is sparse, I keep this low rather than none, but only B is directly relevant to policy handling.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into B’s allowlisted services, policy review is required.
IF retention rules differ between shared files and external services, deletion/export obligations may diverge.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in B workflows.
Document where B sends data.
Set short retention on shared files.
Review vendor terms for allowlisted services.
requires-engineering: formalize residency and retention controls.
